items.title: Decision: kill_command_or_subagent on Grok Build becomes deny-class / attestation-gated. Forever out-of-scope is not a co-equal Prefer-A success. #3987/scheduler_create is the policy-decision pattern; rewriting the audit row alone does not relieve P1.

Enforcement locus (not docs-only): (a) matcher deposit so Grok PreToolUse selects kill_command_or_subagent; (b) dedicated deny-class path (not product-write inspectMutationGates) that reads green attestation before allow, else refuse with printed reason. Docs/host-tool-surface-audit/HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT/preamble update with (a)+(b).

Attestation before kill (parent and peer): prefer deft subagent:pre-cancel exit 0 for that agent_id/attempt when present on tip; equivalent until #5278 lands = recorded .deft-scratch attestation artifact with agent_id, writer_id(=killer), kind in {note,correction,force}, created_at, optional reason, short TTL. Soft English is not attestation. Peer same gate as parent.

Still-running oracle: host task/subagent status non-terminal. Heartbeat STALE/missing or REDISPATCH_OK alone does not reclassify as safe-to-kill-without-attestation. Terminal host status may allow kill without attestation.

Force surface: Directive hook override on kill PreToolUse — allow only with explicit force marker AND non-empty printed reason; if host schema cannot carry force, force lives on attestation (kind:force + reason).

Audit row + preamble: move kill_command_or_subagent off silent forever-OOS process-control into explicit deny-class/attestation-gated record; parents/peers MUST NOT treat documented duty as the kill safety case.

Acceptance/DCR fail-closed: (i) bare kill without attestation refused; (ii) green pre-cancel/equivalent may allow; (iii) force requires non-empty reason and prints it; (iv) peer same as parent; (v) fixture/DCR asserts (i)-(iv) against deny-class path — docs-only checks do not satisfy.

Decision (closes Prefer-A body fork). `kill_command_or_subagent` on Grok Build becomes deny-class / attestation-gated.
Forever out-of-scope is not a co-equal Prefer-A success on this leftover.
#3987 / `scheduler_create` is the policy-decision pattern (deliberate deny-class, not a silent coverage edit into `inspectMutationGates`); rewriting the audit row alone does not relieve P1.

Enforcement locus (not docs-only). Ship both: - (a) Matcher deposit so Grok PreToolUse actually selects `kill_command_or_subagent` (today it is outside mutation catalog and falls through `not-direct-write` allow).
(b) Dedicated deny-class path (not product-write `inspectMutationGates`) that reads a green attestation before allow; otherwise refuse with a printed reason.
Docs / `host-tool-surface-audit.md` / `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT` / preamble updates are required with (a)+(b).
Docs-only wiring reproduces P2.

Attestation before kill (parent and peer). Before allow of host kill on a still-running Grok child, require green attestation: - Prefer: `deft subagent:pre-cancel` exit 0 for that `agent_id` / attempt (same verb #5278 binds for Directive takeover), when that verb exists on the delivery tip.

Equivalent until #5278 lands / if verb absent: a recorded attestation artifact under `.deft-scratch/` with closed schema fields at minimum: `agent_id`, `writer_id` (= killer), `kind` in {note,correction} or `force`, `created_at`, optional `reason`, and a short TTL.
Gate consumer is the deny-class path in (2b).
Soft English "I asked first" is not attestation.
Peer/sibling kill uses the same attestation gate as parent (Stop 1 P1 width).
Still-running oracle. "Still-running" means the host task/subagent status for that id is non-terminal (host-reported running / in-flight).
Heartbeat STALE/missing or REDISPATCH_OK alone does not reclassify the child as safe-to-kill-without-attestation; those paths still go through attestation or explicit force.
Terminal host status may allow kill without attestation (nothing left to protect).

`--force` surface. Force is a Directive hook override on the kill PreToolUse path (not an assumed host CLI flag the tool may never emit): allow only when the tool input / paired attestation carries an explicit force marker and a non-empty printed reason string; the deny path prints that reason on allow-via-force.
If the host tool schema cannot carry force, the force marker lives only on the attestation artifact (`kind: force` + reason) consumed by (2b).

Audit row + preamble. Move `kill_command_or_subagent` off silent forever-OOS "process control" into an explicit deny-class / attestation-gated record (mirror `scheduler_create` known-gap honesty until the gate ships, then record the gated disposition).
Preamble / swarm skill: parents and peers MUST NOT treat documented duty as the kill safety case.
Acceptance / DCR (fail-closed; no soft residual). - (i) Bare host kill of a still-running Grok child without green attestation is refused (hook/DCR), not residual-with-duty.
(ii) Green `subagent:pre-cancel` (or equivalent artifact in item 3) → kill may allow.
(iii) Force path requires non-empty reason and prints it; missing reason stays refuse.
(iv) Peer kill without attestation refuses the same as parent.
(v) Fixture or DCR asserts (i)-(iv) against the deny-class path; document-only checks do not satisfy this item.

(a) Matcher deposit so Grok PreToolUse actually selects `kill_command_or_subagent` (today it is outside mutation catalog and falls through `not-direct-write` allow).

Prefer: `deft subagent:pre-cancel` exit 0 for that `agent_id` / attempt (same verb #5278 binds for Directive takeover), when that verb exists on the delivery tip.
Acceptance / DCR (fail-closed; no soft residual).
(i) Bare host kill of a still-running Grok child without green attestation is refused (hook/DCR), not residual-with-duty.

## Open critique of Prefer-A (host-kill refuse leftover)

Method: pin-read at `dd601935bb21f37df9bf47a3b30954c18505c14f` against Stop 1 P1/P2 (comment 5975633882) and Prefer-A on the issue body. No Bound lean. No synthesis.

### F1 — Prefer-A step 1 keeps a forever-OOS fork that cannot relieve Stop 1

Prefer-A item 1 leaves both outcomes live: `kill_command_or_subagent` stays forever out-of-scope, or it becomes deny-class / attestation-gated.

Stop 1 owns:
- P1 — host kill without attestation on a still-running Grok child
- P2 — out-of-scope document-duty treated as the safety case

A Bound that picks forever-OOS satisfies Prefer-A text while leaving both pains unrelieved by construction. This leftover exists because #5278 Prefer-A deliberately did not claim the host-kill refuse (issue body Why split / Summary). Prefer-A should close the fork: gated deny-class is the relief path; forever-OOS is an explicit non-relief / named residual, not a co-equal Prefer-A success.

### F2 — Enforcement locus is unnamed; pin shows kill is allow-by-default today

At the pin:

- `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT.grok.nonMutation` records `kill_command_or_subagent: "process control"` (`packages/core/src/hooks/tools.ts` ~239).
- Docs mirror that as `out of scope — process control` (`content/docs/host-tool-surface-audit.md` ~50).
- Dispatcher fallthrough for non-direct-write tools returns `verdict: "allow"`, `code: "not-direct-write"`, message that the tool is outside the P0 direct-write/spawn/shell enforcement slice (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts`, `if (!isDirectWriteTool(toolName))` block).

Kill is not in the mutation catalog (`directWrite` / `shell` / `spawn`), so deposited PreToolUse matchers never select it for write/spawn gates. Prefer-A steps 2–3 talk about attestation and docs/audit/preamble, but never name the chokepoint that refuses the host tool.

Concrete gap for a later lean: gating kill is not a coverage edit into `inspectMutationGates` (kill has no product write dest). It needs (a) matcher deposit so PreToolUse fires, plus (b) a dedicated deny path / deny-class that reads attestation, or an explicit host-native refuse. Docs-only wiring (step 3 alone) reproduces P2.

### F3 — `subagent:pre-cancel` is absent at this pin; "or equivalent" is under-specified

Pin-wide grep for `subagent:pre-cancel` / `pre-cancel` attestation surfaces returns no hits under `packages/core` or `content` at `dd601935`. Takeover cancel at this pin is still `task swarm:pre-dispatch -- --action cancel` after REDISPATCH_OK (`content/commands.md` ~362; `content/docs/subagent-heartbeat.md` Takeover after REDISPATCH_OK).

Prefer-A step 2 requires a green `subagent:pre-cancel` attestation (or equivalent) before host kill. That verb is a #5278 deliverable, not a pin fact. Without naming the attestation artifact (path/schema), writer, consumer, TTL, and what "equivalent" means when #5278 has not landed, step 4's DCR/fixture has nothing concrete to assert, and implement can invent a soft check.

### F4 — `--force` reason path is invented relative to the pin

Prefer-A step 2 requires printing a reason on `--force`. Pin tree has no `kill_command_or_subagent` `--force` surface (no schema, hook flag, or CLI flag cite under that name). A lean must say whether force is a host tool argument, a Directive hook override, or deny-message-only — otherwise the acceptance path depends on a flag the host may not emit.

### F5 — `still-running` predicate is unnamed

Prefer-A gates kill of a still-`running` Grok child. Heartbeat docs already distinguish host-reported running from heartbeat liveness / REDISPATCH_OK (`content/docs/subagent-heartbeat.md` Cursor false-alive / OpenClaw sections; commands.md worker liveness). Wrong predicate either blocks kill of host-dark dead children or allows kill while the tool loop is still live. Prefer-A should name the oracle (host task status vs heartbeat `terminal_state` vs delivery-attempt row) before DCR item 4.

### F6 — Step 4 residual escape can re-create the #5278 PA-1 failure

Prefer-A step 4 allows "refused (or explicitly residual with a named control)". Soft residual without a fail-closed machine check is the same document-duty safety case Stop 1 P2 records and that blocked #5278 path-1 (issue body Why split citing PA-1). If residual remains, Prefer-A must require the named control to be a deterministic refuse (hook/DCR), not preamble duty.

### F7 — #3987 precedent is the decision class, not a shipped kill refuse

`scheduler_create` is correctly the deny-class precedent shape: audit text says covering it is "a new deny class that needs a deliberate policy decision rather than a coverage edit (#3987 residual)" (`tools.ts` ~248–251; `host-tool-surface-audit.md` ~57–62). At this pin `scheduler_create` itself remains nonMutation known-gap — still not gated. Prefer-A should treat #3987 as the policy-decision pattern (do not silently coverage-edit), and still require an actual refuse path for kill. Rewriting the kill audit row from "process control" to "known gap" without a deny chokepoint does not relieve P1.

### F8 — Stop 1 peer path is wider than Prefer-A parent wiring

Stop 1 P1 names parent (or peer) invoking host kill. Prefer-A step 3 wires docs/audit/preamble so parents cannot treat documented duty as the safety case. Sibling/peer kill needs the same attestation gate or an explicit non-goal. Leaving peer unstated lets a Bound claim P1 while only constraining parent prose.

### What Prefer-A already gets right

- Leftover ownership of host-kill refuse vs #5278 takeover pre-cancel is correctly scoped; non-goals avoid re-litigating heartbeat wait_kind / Approach 1 arm-probe.
- Citing #3987 as deliberate host-tool deny-class policy (not a matcher tweak) matches the audit's own language for `scheduler_create`.
- Requiring DCR/fixture that bare kill without attestation fails closed is the right acceptance shape if the lean closes the forever-OOS fork and names the chokepoint.

### Steelman

The strongest defense of Prefer-A as written is that step 1's open decision is intentional charter work for the Bound lean, and "or equivalent" / residual are honesty valves so the arc does not over-claim before #5278 lands. That defense holds only if the Bound is forced to pick gated refuse for P1/P2 relief and to name locus + attestation shape; as Prefer-A stands, those valves also admit a non-relieving Bound.

No Bound lean proposed. No synthesis stamp.

## In plain English

Close the forever-out-of-scope fork. Host kill of a still-running Grok child becomes attestation-gated deny-class on Grok Build (#3987-class policy decision), with a real PreToolUse refuse path — not docs-only duty.

## Pain cites (closed form)

relieves: P1
relieves: P2

- P1 covers host kill_command_or_subagent of a still-running Grok child without green pre-cancel attestation (parent or peer)
- P2 covers HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT / docs / preamble treating kill as nonMutation process-control document-duty as the safety case

## Take map

Absorbs round-1 critic 5975652566 F1-F8: close forever-OOS fork (F1); name matcher+deny chokepoint (F2); name attestation artifact / equivalent (F3); name --force surface (F4); name still-running oracle (F5); no soft residual (F6); #3987 as decision-class pattern only (F7); peer same gate as parent (F8).

## Bound remedy

1. **Decision (closes Prefer-A body fork).** `kill_command_or_subagent` on Grok Build becomes **deny-class / attestation-gated**. Forever out-of-scope is **not** a co-equal Prefer-A success on this leftover. #3987 / `scheduler_create` is the **policy-decision pattern** (deliberate deny-class, not a silent coverage edit into `inspectMutationGates`); rewriting the audit row alone does not relieve P1.

2. **Enforcement locus (not docs-only).** Ship both:
   - (a) **Matcher deposit** so Grok PreToolUse actually selects `kill_command_or_subagent` (today it is outside mutation catalog and falls through `not-direct-write` allow).
   - (b) **Dedicated deny-class path** (not product-write `inspectMutationGates`) that reads a green attestation before allow; otherwise refuse with a printed reason.
   Docs / `host-tool-surface-audit.md` / `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT` / preamble updates are required **with** (a)+(b). Docs-only wiring reproduces P2.

3. **Attestation before kill (parent and peer).** Before allow of host kill on a still-running Grok child, require green attestation:
   - Prefer: `deft subagent:pre-cancel` exit 0 for that `agent_id` / attempt (same verb #5278 binds for Directive takeover), when that verb exists on the delivery tip.
   - **Equivalent until #5278 lands / if verb absent:** a recorded attestation artifact under `.deft-scratch/` with closed schema fields at minimum: `agent_id`, `writer_id` (= killer), `kind` in {note,correction} or `force`, `created_at`, optional `reason`, and a short TTL. Gate consumer is the deny-class path in (2b). Soft English "I asked first" is not attestation.
   Peer/sibling kill uses the **same** attestation gate as parent (Stop 1 P1 width).

4. **Still-running oracle.** "Still-running" means the host task/subagent status for that id is non-terminal (host-reported running / in-flight). Heartbeat STALE/missing or REDISPATCH_OK alone does **not** reclassify the child as safe-to-kill-without-attestation; those paths still go through attestation or explicit force. Terminal host status may allow kill without attestation (nothing left to protect).

5. **`--force` surface.** Force is a **Directive hook override** on the kill PreToolUse path (not an assumed host CLI flag the tool may never emit): allow only when the tool input / paired attestation carries an explicit force marker **and** a non-empty printed reason string; the deny path prints that reason on allow-via-force. If the host tool schema cannot carry force, the force marker lives only on the attestation artifact (`kind: force` + reason) consumed by (2b).

6. **Audit row + preamble.** Move `kill_command_or_subagent` off silent forever-OOS "process control" into an explicit deny-class / attestation-gated record (mirror `scheduler_create` known-gap honesty until the gate ships, then record the gated disposition). Preamble / swarm skill: parents and peers MUST NOT treat documented duty as the kill safety case.

7. **Acceptance / DCR (fail-closed; no soft residual).**
   - (i) Bare host kill of a still-running Grok child without green attestation is **refused** (hook/DCR), not residual-with-duty.
   - (ii) Green `subagent:pre-cancel` (or equivalent artifact in item 3) → kill may allow.
   - (iii) Force path requires non-empty reason and prints it; missing reason stays refuse.
   - (iv) Peer kill without attestation refuses the same as parent.
   - (v) Fixture or DCR asserts (i)-(iv) against the deny-class path; document-only checks do not satisfy this item.

## Non-goals (bound)

- Do not re-litigate #5278 takeover pre-cancel / heartbeat wait_kind / Approach 1 arm-probe
- Do not treat unread steer as REDISPATCH_OK (#4286)
- Do not claim that rewriting the audit string alone is P1 relief
- Do not route kill through product-write `inspectMutationGates` as if it had a dest path

## Plain-language summary

Kill of a still-running Grok child becomes a real attestation-gated refuse on Grok Build for parents and peers. Docs change with the gate. Forever out-of-scope is off the table for this leftover.

Stop 1 P1: parent or peer can invoke host `kill_command_or_subagent` on a still-running Grok child with no green pre-cancel attestation (or equivalent) and no printed `--force` reason path.

Bound lean 5975659398 relieves P1 by construction:

1. Item 1 closes the forever-OOS fork; gated deny-class is the only Prefer-A success on this leftover (absorbs round-1 F1).
2. Item 2 names matcher deposit + dedicated deny-class path (not product-write `inspectMutationGates`), so PreToolUse actually selects kill and can refuse (absorbs F2; pin shows today's allow-by-default / no matcher).
3. Item 3 requires green attestation for parent **and** peer, with prefer-`subagent:pre-cancel` when present and a closed equivalent artifact schema under `.deft-scratch/` until #5278 lands (absorbs F3 / F8). Soft English is excluded.
4. Item 4 names the still-running oracle as host task/subagent non-terminal status; heartbeat STALE / REDISPATCH_OK alone do not skip attestation (absorbs F5).

Bound lean 5975659398 relieves P2 by construction:

1. Item 2 requires docs / `host-tool-surface-audit.md` / `HOST_TOOL_SURFACE_AUDIT` / preamble updates **with** matcher+deny path; docs-only wiring is explicitly called out as reproducing P2.
2. Item 6 moves kill off silent forever-OOS "process control" into an explicit deny-class / attestation-gated record, using `#3987` / `scheduler_create` as the **policy-decision pattern only** (absorbs F7); rewriting the audit string alone is a non-goal.

## Summary

Leftover split from design-critique #5278 (parent-steer inbox exists; cancel/kill has no query-first preflight).

#5278 Prefer-A binds a fail-closed **Directive takeover** gate (`subagent:pre-cancel` before `swarm:pre-dispatch --action cancel` / replacement unblock). It deliberately does **not** claim Directive refuses host `kill_command_or_subagent` inside the current recorded `nonMutation` / out-of-scope surface.

This leftover owns the **host-kill refuse** half of Stop 1 P1 on #5278: a deliberate #3987-class policy decision to reclassify or wrap host kill so a still-running Grok child cannot be killed without a pre-cancel attestation (same pattern as merge-path-arm / scheduler_create deny-class precedents).

## Why split

Pain-audit on #5278 (comment 5962633632, PA-1) blocked path-1 when the Prefer-A lean left host-kill as "document parent duty" while still citing `relieves: P1`. Stop 1 owned both surfaces in one pain id. Operator confirmed leftover split 2026-10-02.

## Prefer-A (this leftover)

1. Decide whether `kill_command_or_subagent` stays out-of-scope forever or becomes a deny-class / attestation-gated host tool on Grok Build.
2. If gated: require a green `subagent:pre-cancel` attestation (or equivalent) before host kill of a still-`running` Grok child; print reason on `--force`.
3. Wire docs / host-tool-surface-audit / preamble so parents cannot treat "documented duty" as the safety case.
4. DCR or fixture: bare host kill without attestation is refused (or explicitly residual with a named control).

## Non-goals

- Do not re-litigate #5278 takeover pre-cancel / heartbeat wait_kind / Approach 1 arm-probe (those stay on #5278).
- Do not treat unread steer as REDISPATCH_OK (#4286).
